title: Attainment of the total-variation distance
statement:
Let $\mu$ and $
u$ be probability measures on a measurable space $\Omega$, and let $\mu - 
u$ denote their signed measure difference, with total variation measure $\abs{\mu-
u}$. Then there exists a measurable set $S \subseteq \Omega$ such that
\[
  \abs{\mu(S) - 
u(S)} = 	frac{1}{2}\,\abs{\mu-
u}(\Omega).
\]
hypotheses_covered: mu is a probability measure on the measurable space Omega
nu is a probability measure on the measurable space Omega
replaced:
There exists a measurable set $S \subseteq \Omega$ such that
$|\mu(S) - \nu(S)| = \tfrac{1}{2}\|\mu-\nu\|_{\mathrm{TV}}(\Omega)$.
